question: What is the length of a bacterial cell?
solution:
The correct answer is __**3 to 5 **____**µm**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Cell​
 
 
• Cells are the basic, fundamental unit of life.
 
• So, if we were to break apart an organism to the cellular level, the smallest independent component that we would find would be the cell.
 
• A cell is defined as the smallest, basic unit of life that is responsible for all of life’s processes.
 
• They may be made up of a single cell (unicellular), or many cells (multicellular).
 
• there are two types of cells Prokaryotes and eukaryotes.
 
• Prokaryotes cell size ranges from 0.1 to 9.0 µm in diameter.
 
• The size of the Eukaryotes cells ranges between 10–100 µm in diameter
 
 
 
• Bacteria
 
 
• ​Bacteria are prokaryotic unicellular organisms.
 
• They have a relatively simple cell structure compared to eukaryotic cells.
 
• They also do not possess any membrane-bound organelles such as a nucleus. However, do they possess genetic material (DNA or RNA) in the intracellular space called the nucleoid
 
• Acetobacter aceti and Alicyclobacillus acidophilus are two examples of acidophilic bacteria.
 
• The study of bacteria is called bacteriology.
 
• Four Types of Bacteria are Streptococcus, Bacillus, Actinobacteria, Proteobacteria.
 
• Most bacteria are 0.2μm (micron) in diameter and 2−8μm (micron) in length. Bacterial cells are about one-tenth the size of eukaryotic cells

• Antonie van Leeuwenhoek​
 
 
• He was a trader, land surveyor, wine rower, glassmaker, and microbiologist from the Netherlands.
 
• Van Leeuwenhoek is most known for the microscope he created.
 
• He has made groundbreaking contributions to cell biology and microbiology.
 
• In 1964, microorganisms (bacteria) were detected in a pepper infusion.
 
• A point to note is people did not know about bacteria in the year it was discovered.
 
• Leeuwenhoek called them animalcules.
 
• It was in 1838, that they were called bacteria.​
